candidates.source_name: Trask — Financial Services industry hub (thetrask.com)
candidates.why_relevant: Trask is one of the largest Czech banking-IT integrators. Its financial-services hub names bank clients (Ceska sporitelna, Raiffeisenbank, Slovenska sporitelna) and describes delivered systems (Impresto digital lending, Data-In Open Banking Connector, payments). Because Czech systemic banks are private and never tender publicly, this vendor page is one of very few public records of what technology those banks actually bought. It also carries quantified claims (e.g. a stated share of CZ/SK online payment volume touched by Trask expertise) that can be tracked over time.
candidates.legal_status: public marketing content, copyrighted; facts extractable
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTML fetch + diff of the industry hub and of linked /blog/ case-study slugs; extract client names, product names and quantified claims into an entity-event table.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of seed actor domain; www.trask.cz 301-redirects to www.thetrask.com

candidates.source_name: Trask — Insights / case-study and blog index
candidates.why_relevant: The running index where Trask publishes named bank project write-ups. Observed entries cover J&T Bank digital-channel rebuild, MONETA real-time customer engagement on AWS Kafka/Flink, Raiffeisenbank logging/observability, and a Verification of Payee (VOP) build with Banfico. Case studies and blog posts share the same /blog/<slug> URL space, so a single crawl captures both announcement-grade and technical-detail content. This is the highest-yield single index in the cell for CZ bank technology projects.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the insights index on a weekly cadence, enumerate /blog/ slugs, store new-slug deltas; tag each item with bank entity, technology domain and vendor partner (AWS, Banfico, etc.).
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from Trask homepage navigation

candidates.source_name: Monet+ — Reference (Czech-language client case studies)
candidates.why_relevant: Monet+ (Zlin-Stipa) is the Czech specialist in banking digital identity (ProID) and card/transit payment acceptance (Switchio). Its Czech-language reference list explicitly names CSOB (EMV card acceptance in public transport), Ceska sporitelna (securing Servis24/Business24 internet banking; PKI smartcard network access) and Air Bank (secure internet-banking access). These are concrete, dated public traces of security and payment-acceptance decisions inside private Czech banks that appear nowhere else.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch /reference index + each /reference/<slug> page; parse the Czech client-quote blocks (they carry named bank executives and their titles, useful for the actor map).
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of seed actor domain, then snowball into /reference

candidates.source_name: Monet+ — Novinky (Czech newsroom) and product lines ProID / Switchio
candidates.why_relevant: The Monet+ homepage nav exposes 'Novinky' alongside the two product franchises that matter for this cell: ProID (qualified signatures, certificate lifecycle for banks and insurers) and Switchio (EMV, tokenisation, transit and EV-charging acceptance). Named institutional relationships visible at homepage level include Komercni banka (with an on-record quote from the head of direct-channel development), Raiffeisenbank, Erste Group, PPF and Kooperativa. Tracking the newsroom catches new bank wins before they reach trade press.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Locate the Novinky index from homepage nav (path not yet captured) and add to the weekly diff set alongside /reference.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of seed actor domain

candidates.source_name: Profinit — Case studies index (banking-heavy)
candidates.why_relevant: The densest bank-project disclosure found anywhere in this cell. Individually addressable case studies name Komercni banka (BI partner), Raiffeisenbank (three separate projects: AI campaign targeting, big-data stack, instalment detector), Equa Bank (interest-rate optimiser), Ceska sporitelna (fraud-detection platform), Erste Group Bank (central log monitoring) and M.M.Warburg. Each is effectively a public record of an analytics/risk/fraud programme inside an otherwise opaque private bank, and the Equa Bank item is useful historical evidence given Equa's absorption into Raiffeisenbank CZ.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the index and each /case-studies/<slug>; extract bank entity, capability domain, technology stack and stated outcome metrics into a structured project ledger.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of seed actor domain, then snowball into /case-studies

candidates.source_name: Profinit — Financial Services industry page and Blog/News
candidates.why_relevant: Client-logo wall and positioning page carrying KBC, Erste Group, KB (Komercni banka), Raiffeisen Bank and Berenberg. The logo wall is a cheap, high-signal way to detect new bank relationships (a logo appears before any case study does). The paired /blog/ index adds commentary that often previews regulatory-driven build programmes (DORA, instant payments, VoP).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Diff the rendered logo/client set and the blog index monthly; alert on new financial-institution logos.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from Profinit homepage navigation

candidates.source_name: Adastra — Success stories (EN and CS)
candidates.why_relevant: Adastra's portfolio sitemap exposes a banking-heavy success-story set: a robotic branch assistant at Tatra banka, automatic categorisation of ~98.5% of card transactions, Raiffeisenbank internet-banking response-time work with Dynatrace, an unnamed 'leading bank' data-management concept, MetLife paperless applications, and event-driven marketing in banking. Crucially, every story exists in a Czech mirror under /cs/success-stories/, so this satisfies local-language coverage for Adastra. The anonymised 'leading bank' items are themselves intelligence: they signal deals the bank refused to be named in.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll https://adastracorp.com/avada_portfolio-sitemap.xml (WordPress/Avada portfolio sitemap) for new slugs — far cheaper and more complete than crawling the JS-heavy index — then fetch the EN and /cs/ variants of each new slug.
candidates.discovered_via_method: adastra.cz 301 -> adastracorp.com/cs/; then sitemap.xml -> avada_portfolio-sitemap.xml snowball

candidates.source_name: Aricoma — Our customers, Banks & Insurance filter
candidates.why_relevant: Aricoma (KKCG technology division, ~EUR 500m revenue, 6000+ staff) publishes a filterable customer wall with an explicit 'Banks and Insurance Companies' branch. Named financial customers observed: CSOB Group, Ceska sporitelna, Raiffeisenbank, ING Management Services, Citibank, plus Kooperativa, UNIQA, Simplea, Home Credit, Broker Consulting and SATUM. For the largest Czech integrator this customer wall is the only systematic public statement of which banks it serves, and Aricoma is a roll-up so the wall changes as it acquires.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch with the branch filter applied and snapshot the customer set; diff quarterly to detect additions/removals after Aricoma acquisitions.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of seed actor domain, snowball through nav

candidates.source_name: Aricoma — Tiskove zpravy (Czech press releases)
candidates.why_relevant: Full Czech-language mirror of the Aricoma newsroom (URL pattern /cs/tiskove-zpravy/<slug>, EN mirror at /press-releases/<slug>). This is the disclosure channel for Aricoma's M&A and, when banks permit it, for named bank projects. Recent output observed is M&A-dominated (Dentsu Tracking acquisition 01/08/2026; SAP suppliers in Austria and Slovenia 08/01/2026; SAP consolidation 01/01/2026) which is itself relevant: it maps how Czech bank-IT supply is consolidating under KKCG.
candidates.legal_status: corporate press releases, intended for redistribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly diff of both /cs/tiskove-zpravy and /press-releases indexes; pair CS/EN slugs so the Czech wording (often richer on client detail) is the extraction target.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from aricoma.com nav; CS path inferred from the site's /cs/home language switch and confirmed by fetch

candidates.source_name: KKCG — Investors and Group news (Aricoma's parent)
candidates.why_relevant: KKCG is an investment group (stated 40+ countries, EUR 1.5bn+ EBITDA, 16,000+ employees) whose Technology division contains Aricoma. Because Aricoma itself is not separately listed, the parent's investor disclosures and news feed are the closest thing to audited, periodic reporting on the largest Czech bank-IT integrator — division revenue, acquisitions and strategy. The news feed exposes a machine-readable RSS endpoint.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Subscribe to the RSS feed at https://www.kkcg.com/en/news/feed.xml; separately poll /en/investors for report PDFs and archive them with hash + retrieval date.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from Aricoma 'We Are Part of KKCG' -> kkcg.com

candidates.source_name: ICZ Group — Reference (incl. CEBIS for Ceska exportni banka)
candidates.why_relevant: ICZ's Czech-language reference section carries a filterable 'Bankovnictvi' / 'Pojistovnictvi' vertical. The concrete banking reference observed is CEBIS, a bespoke commercial-case origination and approval system for CEB (Ceska exportni banka) covering loans, guarantees, purchased receivables and syndicated/club deals — a rare public description of an origination platform at a state-owned Czech bank. Adjacent insurance/pension references (Dovera, VsZP, Union, STABILITA) map ICZ's document-management franchise across CZ/SK financial institutions.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl /reference/ with the bankovnictvi and pojistovnictvi filters; because CEB is a state-owned bank, cross-reference each ICZ reference against Registr smluv and NEN to recover contract values.
candidates.discovered_via_method: i.cz 301 -> iczgroup.com; snowball through Czech nav

candidates.source_name: ICZ Group — Aktuality (Czech newsroom)
candidates.why_relevant: Dated Czech-language news stream (items observed through July 2026) covering product launches, certifications and events. ICZ is diversified into ATM/air-traffic, logistics and public sector, so banking items are sparse — but the feed is the vendor's only chronological disclosure channel and is where a bank-project announcement would first appear. Czech is the primary language with EN and SK mirrors.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly index diff with a Czech-keyword filter (banka, bankovni, pojistovna, platebni, uverovy) to suppress the dominant non-financial output.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from iczgroup.com nav

candidates.source_name: Avenga — Success stories and News (successor domain of Cleverlance)
candidates.why_relevant: IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE CELL BRIEF: www.cleverlance.com issues a 301 redirect to www.avenga.com, not to Aricoma. Cleverlance's Czech banking-integration practice therefore has to be tracked through Avenga, which retains Prague, Brno and Ostrava offices and lists financial clients including Raiffeisen Bank, UniCredit, Generali, Fidelity, Bank of Cyprus and Marginalen Bank. Missing this redirect would leave a large slice of Czech bank-IT delivery history uncovered.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl /success/ and /news/ filtered to financial services; separately query the Czech commercial register for the Cleverlance legal entity to establish the ownership chain and whether a CZ entity still files locally.
candidates.discovered_via_method: fetch of cleverlance.com returned 301 -> avenga.com; verified Avenga homepage

candidates.source_name: Unicorn — corporate site and news archive (unicorn.com)
candidates.why_relevant: Unicorn (tagline 'Tvorime digitalni budoucnost') is a major Czech software house with long-running banking delivery. Its sitemap confirms a full trilingual structure (root, /en/, /cs/) with ~168 URLs, a news archive (news-archiv-unicorn-all, news-detail) and product pages for Unicorn Universe, but NO dedicated case-study/reference section and NO investor-relations section were present in the sitemap. The site is client-side rendered, so plain HTTP fetches return only the title element — collection needs a headless browser.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Headless-browser render (Playwright) of /cs/ news-detail pages; use https://unicorn.com/sitemap.xml as the change-detection primitive since it enumerates all three language variants. unicornsystems.eu 301-redirects here, so treat it as an alias not a separate source.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of seed actor; unicornsystems.eu 301 -> unicorn.com; sitemap.xml enumeration
candidates.observed_blocker: HTTP fetch of unicorn.com and unicorn.com/cz returns only the <title> element; body content is client-side rendered. unicorn.com/cz returned 404 (Czech path is /cs/).

candidates.source_name: Asseco Central Europe — corporate site / newsroom
candidates.why_relevant: Asseco Central Europe is a core-banking and financial-software supplier across CZ/SK and the single most important named actor in this cell for core-system disclosure. The legacy domain www.asseco-ce.com issues a 302 to ce.asseco.com, confirming the domain migration. Both ce.asseco.com/ and ce.asseco.com/en/news/ returned HTTP 403 to a plain fetch — the strong hypothesis is bot defence (WAF/Cloudflare) on a live site, NOT a dead host. Do not record as dead; re-attempt with a browser-grade client.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Retry with a headless browser carrying a realistic UA and TLS fingerprint; also probe ce.asseco.com/robots.txt and /sitemap.xml which WAFs commonly leave open, to recover the CS/EN newsroom path before crawling.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of seed actor domain; observed 302 from legacy domain then 403 at target
candidates.observed_blocker: HTTP 403 Forbidden at https://ce.asseco.com/ and at https://ce.asseco.com/en/news/ (no body returned). Legacy https://www.asseco-ce.com/cz/ returns 302 to https://ce.asseco.com/.

candidates.source_name: Asseco Poland — Investor Relations (listed parent of Asseco Central Europe)
candidates.why_relevant: Asseco Poland is WSE-listed and consolidates the Central Europe segment, so its periodic and current reports are the only audited, regulator-grade financial disclosure touching Czech banking-software revenue in this cell. Segment notes and management commentary are where Czech banking-sector performance would be quantified. Not yet reachable: https://asseco.com/investor-relations/ and https://inwestor.asseco.com/en/ both returned HTTP 403 to plain fetch — again a bot-defence hypothesis, not a dead-site verdict.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Headless-browser retry; if still blocked, obtain the same filings from the regulated distribution channel (WSE/ESPI-EBI current and periodic reports) rather than the issuer website, which is the more durable collection path anyway.
candidates.discovered_via_method: inferred parent of Asseco Central Europe; direct fetch attempts
candidates.observed_blocker: HTTP 403 Forbidden at both https://asseco.com/investor-relations/ and https://inwestor.asseco.com/en/ (no body returned).

candidates.source_name: GEM System — corporate site
candidates.why_relevant: Named seed actor for this cell (Czech IT services with financial-sector delivery). Could not be characterised: https://www.gemsystem.cz/, https://gemsystem.cz/, https://www.gemsystem.cz/cz/ and https://www.gemsystem.cz/robots.txt all terminated with 'too many redirects (exceeded 10)'. That pattern usually indicates a misconfigured www/non-www or language-cookie redirect loop against a cookieless client, or a locale negotiation loop — the host resolves and responds, so it is very likely live. Retain as a target and re-attempt with cookie support.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Re-fetch with a cookie jar and Accept-Language: cs enabled (headless browser), which normally breaks locale-negotiation loops; if it persists, confirm the current corporate domain via the Czech commercial register entry for GEM System a.s.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of seed actor domain (four URL variants attempted)
candidates.observed_blocker: 'Too many redirects (exceeded 10)' on https://www.gemsystem.cz/, https://gemsystem.cz/, https://www.gemsystem.cz/cz/ and https://www.gemsystem.cz/robots.txt.

candidates.source_name: CCA Group — Reference and Novinky
candidates.why_relevant: Named seed actor, verified live with a clean Czech structure (/reference/, /novinky/, /o-spolecnosti/, service pages for custom software, application maintenance, customer support and cybersecurity; 100+ staff, 30+ years). However its published references are public-sector and industrial — Ministry of Justice information systems since 1995, the Czech Office for Surveying and Cadastre, the Ministry of Finance gambling-oversight system AISG, and SKODA JS ERP — with no banking clients visible. Keep at low-frequency monitoring: it is a plausible bidder on state-owned bank work but is not currently a bank-technology disclosure channel.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency (quarterly) diff of /reference/ and /novinky/ with a banking keyword trigger; do not spend crawl budget here otherwise.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of seed actor domain

candidates.source_name: SystemOnLine.cz — IT pro banky a financni organizace (vertical) + IT vendor directory
candidates.why_relevant: The single best Czech-language pointer source for this cell. SystemOnLine (publisher of the IT Systems magazine) runs a dedicated banking/financial-organisations vertical that republishes vendor case studies and bylined vendor articles, AND maintains a supplier directory (dodavatele IT sluzeb a reseni) plus product overviews covering 77+ ERP and 51+ CRM vendors. That directory is the snowball engine for discovering bank-IT vendors outside the ten seed actors. Note the bare domain systemonline.cz fails TLS hostname validation — always use the www host.
candidates.legal_status: trade publication, copyrighted; use for pointer extraction and citation
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the banking vertical index and /zpravy/ for new items; separately harvest /dodavatele-it-sluzeb-a-reseni/ once per quarter to expand the vendor actor map, then feed newly discovered vendors back into per-vendor newsroom monitoring.
candidates.discovered_via_method: inferred category (Czech enterprise-IT trade portal), confirmed by fetch and nav snowball
local_language_terms_used: IT pro banky a financni organizace

candidates.source_name: Bankovnictvi (casopis) — Technologie section
candidates.why_relevant: The Czech banking trade magazine (published by 4H production s.r.o., Prague) with a standing Technologie rubric alongside Banky a finance, Produkty a sluzby, Regulace, Rozhovory and Personalie. It is the demand-side mirror of the vendor newsrooms in this cell: where a vendor claims a win, Bankovnictvi often carries the bank's own framing, plus executive interviews and personnel moves that identify the decision-makers behind technology spend. Freemium — free previews with a subscription tier.
candidates.legal_status: copyrighted trade publication; respect paywall, collect metadata and free previews only
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll /technologie, /banky-finance and /personalie indexes for headlines and dates; store metadata plus free preview text. Do not circumvent the subscription wall — treat paywalled bodies as a licensing decision.
candidates.discovered_via_method: inferred category (national banking trade press), confirmed by fetch

candidates.source_name: Computertrends.cz (successor of Computerworld.cz, IDG/iinfo network)
candidates.why_relevant: Czech IT-professional daily ('Denik pro IT profesionaly') carrying a Press Room stream of vendor announcements plus analysis (/analyzy-a-studie/) and security (/securityworld/) sections. Note the domain migration: www.computerworld.cz now issues a 301 to www.computertrends.cz — any historical link set pointing at computerworld.cz needs rewriting. Useful as a secondary confirmation channel when a vendor claims a bank project, and for catching smaller integrators that never issue their own press release.
candidates.access_status: mostly open, hybrid subscription for magazine content
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl section indexes with a Czech banking keyword filter (banka, bankovni system, platebni, core banking, pojistovna); an RSS endpoint was not confirmed, so plan on index diffing.
candidates.discovered_via_method: fetch of computerworld.cz returned 301 -> computertrends.cz

candidates.source_name: Lupa.cz — Czech internet and digital-infrastructure daily
candidates.why_relevant: Long-running Czech portal ('server o ceskem Internetu') with Clanky, Aktuality, Video, Podcast and a Lupa+ premium tier. Coverage observed spans Czech IT vendors and startups, banking/fintech infrastructure (including digital certificate systems and cloud platforms) and government digitalisation. Lupa frequently reports vendor-bank stories with independent scepticism, which is exactly the corrective needed when the only other record is a vendor's own case study.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword-filtered monitoring of Clanky and Aktuality on the ten seed vendor names plus Czech bank names; an RSS URL was not confirmed on the homepage, so verify a feed path before assuming one.
candidates.discovered_via_method: inferred category (Czech tech news), confirmed by fetch

candidates.source_name: ICT UNIE — member register of Czech IT and electronic-communications firms
candidates.why_relevant: Czech ICT trade association ('Profesni sdruzeni firem z oboru IT informacnich technologii a elektronickych komunikaci') publishing a member list of roughly 60 companies with logos, an Aktuality stream, a 'V mediich' clippings section, working groups and sector statistics drawn from the Czech Statistical Office. This is the cheapest way to complete the vendor actor map beyond the ten seed names and to pick up the sector-level aggregates that contextualise individual vendor wins.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off harvest of /clenove-ictu to seed the vendor entity list, then quarterly re-harvest for membership deltas; subscribe to /aktuality for association statements and CSU-derived digitalisation statistics.
candidates.discovered_via_method: inferred category (who represents/aggregates the vendor population), confirmed by fetch

candidates.source_name: Registr smluv (smlouvy.gov.cz) — mandatory Czech contracts registry
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory registry under Act No. 340/2015 Sb., live since 1 July 2016, administered since 1 April 2023 by the Digital and Information Agency (DIA). Contracts in scope must be published within 30 days of execution or they are void. For this cell it converts vendor marketing claims into evidenced, valued contracts wherever the counterparty is a state-controlled financial institution (e.g. Ceska exportni banka, Narodni rozvojova banka) or a public body buying payment/banking systems — precisely the ICZ CEBIS class of project. Advanced search at /vyhledavani; an Open Data section and an IS description page are published.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the Open Data / IS interface rather than the HTML UI: standing queries by supplier ICO for each of the ten seed vendors, plus by state-owned-bank counterparty; store contract value, subject text and PDF annexes.
candidates.discovered_via_method: inferred category (who must publish / who archives), confirmed by fetch

candidates.source_name: Hlidac statu — aggregated contracts, tenders and subsidies with API/MCP access
candidates.why_relevant: Independent Czech watchdog (self-described as the country's largest, 10 years running, donor-funded, no state money or advertising) that indexes 8.5m contracts, 1.5m public tenders, subsidies and official salaries. Its value over the raw Registr smluv is queryability and entity resolution: it offers a documented API (api.hlidacstatu.cz) and an MCP server endpoint (mcp.api.hlidacstatu.cz), all free of charge. This is the practical way to run standing supplier-side queries for Asseco, Trask, Adastra, ICZ, Unicorn, CCA, Aricoma and Profinit against every public counterparty at once.
candidates.access_status: open, free API (registration likely required for a key)
candidates.legal_status: civic open-data project; check API terms and attribution requirement before systematic use
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Register for an API key at api.hlidacstatu.cz and run scheduled supplier-ICO queries across /smlouvy and /verejnezakazky; the MCP endpoint at mcp.api.hlidacstatu.cz allows agent-native querying without a bespoke client.
candidates.discovered_via_method: inferred category (who aggregates/archives public disclosure), confirmed by fetch

candidates.source_name: NEN / NIPEZ — Narodni elektronicky nastroj (public procurement) and ISVZ statistics
candidates.why_relevant: The national electronic tool for administering and publishing Czech public contracts and concessions, reporting 22,486 contracting authorities, 41,555 suppliers, 269,324 realised contracts and CZK 2,119bn in value. It links to the Vestnik verejnych zakazek (procurement gazette) and to ISVZ statistical reporting at isvz.nipez.cz/reporty. Directly relevant to this cell wherever a state-owned or public financial institution procures banking technology, and it also yields supplier-side profiles for the seed vendors, revealing public-sector revenue concentration that private vendors do not otherwise disclose.
candidates.legal_status: official public procurement system, open data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Supplier-name and CPV-code standing searches; pull aggregate series from https://isvz.nipez.cz/reporty. A documented bulk API was not confirmed on the homepage — check https://podpora.nipez.cz before assuming one exists.
candidates.discovered_via_method: inferred category (who regulates/records public buying), confirmed by fetch

candidates.source_name: Verejny rejstrik a Sbirka listin (or.justice.cz) — vendor annual reports and financial statements
candidates.why_relevant: The Ministry of Justice public register with the Sbirka listin (collection of deeds). Every one of the ten seed vendors is a Czech legal entity obliged to file annual accounts and, where applicable, a vyrocni zprava. Because Trask, Monet+, Adastra CZ, Profinit, ICZ, CCA, GEM System and Unicorn are all privately held with no investor-relations function, these statutory filings are the ONLY audited financial disclosure available on them — the counterweight to unverifiable marketing claims, and the way to size Czech bank technology spend from the supply side. Search by company name or ICO; a redesigned register is in testing at verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz.
candidates.access_status: open (no authentication for basic and advanced search)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Resolve each seed vendor to an ICO (cross-check against ARES), then pull the Sbirka listin PDF set annually; archive with retrieval date. PDF availability and any open-data/API route were not confirmed on the search page — verify before building the pipeline, and evaluate the new verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz interface as the longer-term target.
candidates.discovered_via_method: inferred category (who must file / who archives), confirmed by fetch

negative_findings.description: The session's WebSearch budget was already fully consumed (200 of 200 calls) before this cell began. Every planned Czech-language and English seed query — 'Asseco Central Europe tiskova zprava banka implementace', 'Trask Solutions pripadova studie banka reference', and the remaining seed and extension queries — was refused by the tool with a budget message, not executed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero search queries executed. All discovery in this slice was performed by direct URL fetching of seed-actor domains, sitemap enumeration, redirect-chain following and navigation snowballing. The queries_used field is therefore empty on every candidate — this is an honest empty, not an omission.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The routine mandates local-language search. Fetch-and-snowball recovers the known actors and their structures well, but it cannot surface unknown vendors, one-off press releases carried only by third parties, or bank-project stories on sites nobody thought to guess. Recall in this cell should be assumed materially below what a searched run would achieve, and the cell should be re-run with search budget available.

negative_findings.description: The coverage cell pairs 'Aricoma/Cleverlance' as one actor. A fetch of https://www.cleverlance.com/ returned HTTP 301 to https://www.avenga.com/ — not to Aricoma. Avenga's own site lists Prague, Brno and Ostrava offices and financial clients including Raiffeisen Bank, UniCredit, Generali and Fidelity.
negative_findings.result_summary: Cleverlance's web identity now resolves to Avenga, a separate group from Aricoma/KKCG. Aricoma (aricoma.com, KKCG technology division) is a distinct live actor with its own newsroom and customer wall.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Treating Cleverlance as an Aricoma sub-brand would silently drop a whole delivery organisation with substantial Czech banking history from the monitored set, and would mis-attribute past Cleverlance bank projects to the wrong corporate parent. Both aricoma.com and avenga.com must be tracked separately.

negative_findings.description: Trask appears to have retired its Czech-language web presence. https://www.trask.cz/ issues a 301 to https://www.thetrask.com/, and both https://www.thetrask.com/cs and https://www.thetrask.com/cz returned HTTP 404. All observed navigation and content paths use the /en/ prefix.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Czech-language Trask site path was found. Trask content is collected in English only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Trask is the single richest source of Czech bank project disclosure in this cell, yet it now publishes in English only. Anyone monitoring by Czech keywords alone will miss it entirely, and Czech-language name variants of banks (e.g. 'Ceska sporitelna' vs 'Ceska Sporitelna'/'CS') will not match. Monitoring rules for Trask must be English-keyword-based, which is the opposite of the default assumption for a Czech vendor.

negative_findings.description: CCA Group (cca.cz) is live and well-structured in Czech, but its published reference set contains no banking or financial-institution clients. Observed references are the Ministry of Justice (information systems since 1995), the Czech Office for Surveying and Cadastre, the Ministry of Finance gambling-oversight system AISG, and SKODA JS ERP.
negative_findings.result_summary: CCA Group verified as a live actor but not currently a bank-technology disclosure channel; it reads as a public-sector and industrial custom-software house.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell definition assumes all ten seed vendors are bank-technology suppliers. At least one is not, on its own public evidence. Spending equal crawl budget across all ten would waste effort; CCA should drop to low-frequency keyword-triggered monitoring rather than routine collection.

negative_findings.description: Aricoma's press-release stream carries no banking items in its recent output. The three most recent releases observed on both the EN (/press-releases) and CS (/cs/tiskove-zpravy) indexes are the Dentsu Tracking acquisition (01/08/2026), the acquisition of SAP suppliers in Austria and Slovenia (08/01/2026) and the consolidation of its SAP companies (01/01/2026). Separately, the /case-studies index exposes a 'Banks and Insurance Companies' branch filter but the default listing surfaced no banking case studies among 20+ visible items.
negative_findings.result_summary: Aricoma's banking relationships are visible on its customer wall (CSOB Group, Ceska sporitelna, Raiffeisenbank, ING, Citibank) but are not narrated in recent press releases or in the unfiltered case-study listing.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For Czech bank projects Aricoma discloses relationships, not projects — the customer wall carries the signal while the newsroom carries M&A. Collection should weight the customer wall and the filtered case-study view over the press feed, and the filtered branch view must be fetched explicitly because the default listing hides it.

negative_findings.description: Asseco properties refused plain HTTP fetches. https://ce.asseco.com/ and https://ce.asseco.com/en/news/ both returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with no body; https://asseco.com/investor-relations/ and https://inwestor.asseco.com/en/ likewise returned 403. The legacy domain https://www.asseco-ce.com/cz/ returned a 302 to ce.asseco.com, confirming an intentional, maintained domain migration.
negative_findings.result_summary: Asseco Central Europe and Asseco Poland IR are recorded as unverified-blocked, NOT dead. A maintained 302 from the legacy domain is positive evidence the estate is live and actively managed; a blanket 403 across four unrelated paths on two hosts is the signature of a WAF, not of removed content.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Asseco Central Europe is arguably the most important single actor in this cell — a core-banking supplier across CZ/SK whose parent is WSE-listed and therefore subject to audited segment disclosure. Losing it to a premature 'dead' verdict would gut the cell. Re-attempt with a headless browser; if the issuer site stays blocked, route to the regulated WSE/ESPI filing channel, which is the more durable path regardless.

negative_findings.description: GEM System could not be characterised. Four URL variants — https://www.gemsystem.cz/, https://gemsystem.cz/, https://www.gemsystem.cz/cz/ and https://www.gemsystem.cz/robots.txt — all terminated with 'too many redirects (exceeded 10)'.
negative_findings.result_summary: GEM System recorded as unverified with a redirect-loop blocker. The host resolves and responds at every variant, so the site is very likely live; the loop pattern is characteristic of www/non-www or locale negotiation failing against a cookieless client.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: One of ten seed actors is entirely uncharacterised, so its banking references (if any) are unknown. The failure mode is a client limitation rather than a source problem, which means it is cheaply fixable with a cookie-enabled headless fetch — it should not be written off.

negative_findings.description: Unicorn's sitemap (https://unicorn.com/sitemap.xml, ~168 URLs across root, /en/ and /cs/ prefixes) contains news pages (news-archiv-unicorn-all, news-detail, news-coworkers), company pages (unicorn-group-profile, mission, history), service pages and product pages (Unicorn Universe), but NO dedicated case-study/reference section and NO investor-relations section. Plain fetches of unicorn.com, unicorn.com/cz and the EN news archive returned only the page title because the site is client-side rendered; unicorn.com/cz returned 404 (the Czech prefix is /cs/).
negative_findings.result_summary: Unicorn publishes no public reference or case-study library and no IR section on this domain, and what it does publish is not retrievable without JavaScript execution. unicornsystems.eu 301-redirects to unicorn.com, so it is an alias rather than a second source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Unicorn is a large Czech software house with known banking delivery, but it is structurally silent about named clients on the open web — so for this actor the vendor-newsroom channel that underpins the whole cell rationale does not function. Coverage of Unicorn's bank work must come from other channels: Sbirka listin filings, procurement records, and trade press. It also warns that sitemap presence, not homepage fetch, is the only reliable change-detection primitive for JS-rendered vendor sites.

negative_findings.description: Four of the cell's relevant domains have migrated and answer only via redirect: www.trask.cz 301 to www.thetrask.com; www.i.cz 301 to www.iczgroup.com; adastra.cz and www.adastragrp.com to adastracorp.com (and /cs/); www.computerworld.cz 301 to www.computertrends.cz. Separately, the bare host systemonline.cz fails TLS certificate validation ('not in the cert's altnames') and only www.systemonline.cz is usable.
negative_findings.result_summary: Legacy domain lists for this cell are stale. All redirects observed were single-hop and well-formed, so the underlying sources are healthy — only the addresses changed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any historical source registry or monitoring config built on the old domains will either fail or silently follow redirects without updating provenance, corrupting the audit trail. The systemonline.cz TLS mismatch in particular produces a hard failure that looks like a dead source but is only a hostname error — always store the www form.

negative_findings.description: An attempt to locate the Czech National Bank's public procurement page at https://www.cnb.cz/cs/o_cnb/verejne-zakazky/ returned HTTP 404. The correct path for the CNB profil zadavatele was not established within this slice, and no CNB procurement URL is asserted.
negative_findings.result_summary: No CNB procurement source recorded. This is a negative finding rather than a guessed URL.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The CNB is both a bank and a contracting authority, so its supplier awards are one of the few fully public records of a Czech bank buying technology — a direct complement to this cell's vendor-side sources. The gap is a missed high-value channel, not a dead end; the correct path needs to be found via the CNB site navigation or the procurement gazette.

coverage_gaps.description: Mandatory Czech-language (and English) search was not performed at all because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before the cell started. Every seed query and every planned extension query went unrun; discovery relied entirely on fetching known domains, following redirects and enumerating sitemaps.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run this cell with search budget available (raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION or allocate the cell its own session). Execute the six seed queries plus Czech extensions such as 'implementace jadroveho bankovniho systemu banka CR dodavatel', 'referencni zakaznik banka IT integrator Ceska republika', 'migrace core banking system tiskova zprava', 'dodavatel platebnich systemu banka reference', and site-scoped queries against systemonline.cz and bankovnictvionline.cz.

coverage_gaps.description: Two of the ten named seed actors remain uncharacterised or structurally silent: GEM System (redirect loop on all four URL variants attempted) and Unicorn (JS-rendered; sitemap shows no reference or investor section). Asseco Central Europe, the most important actor in the cell, is 403-blocked.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Deploy a headless browser (Playwright) with a cookie jar, Accept-Language: cs and a realistic user agent for gemsystem.cz, unicorn.com and ce.asseco.com. For Asseco also probe /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml, which WAFs usually leave reachable, to recover the newsroom paths before crawling.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell's ten seed vendors are almost certainly not the full Czech bank-technology supplier population. No systematic expansion was performed, and one seed actor (CCA Group) turned out to have no banking references at all — evidence the list was assembled by reputation rather than from a register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Harvest https://www.ictu.cz/clenove-ictu (approx. 60 members) and https://www.systemonline.cz/dodavatele-it-sluzeb-a-reseni/ as the two authoritative vendor registers, then intersect with supplier names appearing in Registr smluv and NEN against financial-sector counterparties. Promote any vendor with a banking reference into per-vendor newsroom monitoring, and demote CCA Group to keyword-triggered monitoring only.

coverage_gaps.description: No demand-side public-buyer channel for state-controlled Czech financial institutions was successfully captured. The CNB procurement page 404'd on the path attempted, and no profil zadavatele was located for Ceska exportni banka (CEB) or Narodni rozvojova banka (NRB, formerly CMZRB) — even though the ICZ CEBIS reference proves CEB buys bespoke banking systems.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate the profil zadavatele for CNB, CEB and NRB via the Vestnik verejnych zakazek and NEN rather than by guessing site paths, then add each as a standing source. Cross-reference every awarded supplier against the vendor actor map to convert vendor marketing claims into valued, dated contracts.

coverage_gaps.description: Non-web vendor disclosure channels were not examined at all: vendor LinkedIn company pages (where Czech integrators often announce bank wins before or instead of a press release), conference programmes and recorded talks (e.g. banking-IT conferences where bank CIOs present their vendor stack), vendor YouTube channels, and job postings that name the specific core-banking or payment platform a vendor is staffing for a named bank.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add LinkedIn company-page monitoring for the seed vendors, and treat Czech IT job boards (jobs.cz, and vendor career sites such as icz.jobs.cz and jsmeprofinit.eu) as a leading indicator: required-skills fields frequently disclose the bank platform in flight months ahead of any case study.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor financial disclosure was identified as a channel (Sbirka listin, KKCG investor pages) but no actual filing was retrieved, and no vendor was resolved to an ICO in this slice. PDF availability and any open-data/API route for or.justice.cz were not confirmed on the search page.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Resolve each of the ten seed vendors to an ICO via ARES, pull the Sbirka listin document list per entity, and confirm whether PDFs are directly addressable or require session-bound navigation. Evaluate the redesigned register at https://verejnerejstriky.msp.gov.cz/ as the longer-term collection target, and confirm CZ-entity filing status for the Avenga/Cleverlance and Adastra Czech legal entities specifically.

coverage_gaps.description: Local-language coverage is uneven across the cell in a way that defeats a single monitoring rule. Monet+, ICZ and CCA publish primarily in Czech; Aricoma, Adastra and Unicorn maintain true CS/EN mirrors (/cs/tiskove-zpravy, /cs/success-stories/, /cs/); Trask and Profinit publish in English only despite being Czech companies; Asseco's language structure is unknown because the site is blocked.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Maintain per-source language profiles rather than one cell-wide keyword set. Run bilingual entity aliases for every bank (e.g. Ceska sporitelna / Czech Savings Bank / CS, Komercni banka / KB, Ceskoslovenska obchodni banka / CSOB, Ceska exportni banka / CEB, Narodni rozvojova banka / NRB) and prefer the /cs/ variant for extraction where a mirror exists, since Czech texts observed carried richer client detail and named executives.

brief: Czech bank-technology vendors function exactly as the cell rationale predicts: with the systemic banks private and their procurement invisible, the supplier's own case-study library is the public record, and four vendors carry almost all of it — Profinit (named projects at Komercni banka, Ceska sporitelna, Raiffeisenbank, Equa Bank and Erste Group), Trask (J&T Bank, MONETA, Raiffeisenbank, Ceska sporitelna, plus the Impresto lending and Verification-of-Payee lines), Adastra (Tatra banka, Raiffeisenbank and card-transaction categorisation, mirrored in Czech at /cs/success-stories/) and Monet+ (CSOB, Ceska sporitelna and Air Bank on digital identity and card acceptance). Aricoma discloses relationships rather than projects — its customer wall names CSOB Group, Ceska sporitelna, Raiffeisenbank, ING and Citibank while its newsroom is M&A-dominated — and ICZ contributes the rare state-owned-bank artefact in CEBIS for Ceska exportni banka. Three structural cautions shape collection: Cleverlance now redirects to Avenga rather than Aricoma, so a whole delivery organisation sits outside the cell as briefed; CCA Group publishes no banking references at all; and Unicorn, GEM System and Asseco Central Europe are silent, loop-blocked and 403-blocked respectively, the latter two being client-side limitations rather than dead sources. Because vendor claims are self-reported marketing, the cell should be anchored on three neutral spines — Registr smluv and Hlidac statu's free API for contracts, NEN for public procurement, and the Sbirka listin for the audited accounts that are the only financial disclosure these privately held vendors ever make — with SystemOnLine's banking vertical and vendor directory as the snowball engine for the actors the seed list missed.
